subject: ela
intro: This test covers the whole Key Ideas and Details cluster for grade 4 literature across all three standards: referring to details and drawing inferences with evidence (4.RL.A.1), determining theme and summarizing (4.RL.A.2), and describing characters, settings, and events in depth (4.RL.A.3). Each question is multiple choice and labeled with the standard it checks.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

Max packed a water bottle, tied his cleats, and grabbed the black-and-white ball on his way out the door.

Where is Max most likely going?
A) To a soccer game or practice
B) To the library
C) To bed
D) To a swimming pool
items.answer: A) To a soccer game or practice

steps: The clues are cleats and a black-and-white ball.
Those are soccer items.
So Max is going to soccer, choice A.
solution.answer: A) To a soccer game or practice

items.prompt:
Read the story.

Because the school lost power in the storm, the classes moved to the gym, where the big windows let in daylight.

Why did the classes move to the gym?
A) The gym was warmer
B) The school lost power, so they needed the daylight from the windows
C) It was time for recess
D) The teachers wanted to play games
items.answer: B) The school lost power, so they needed the daylight from the windows

steps: The question asks why they moved.
The story says the school "lost power" and the gym had "big windows."
They moved for the daylight, choice B.
solution.answer: B) The school lost power, so they needed the daylight from the windows

items.prompt:
Read the story.

When Jonah opened his lunchbox, he found a note in his mother's handwriting and his favorite cookies, even though it was an ordinary Tuesday. He smiled and tucked the note into his pocket instead of throwing it away.

What can you infer about how Jonah feels about the note?
A) He is annoyed by it
B) He treasures it because he keeps it in his pocket
C) He did not notice it
D) He wants to trade it
items.answer: B) He treasures it because he keeps it in his pocket

steps: Jonah smiles at the note and tucks it in his pocket.
He keeps it instead of throwing it away.
That shows he treasures it, choice B.
solution.answer: B) He treasures it because he keeps it in his pocket

items.prompt:
Read the story.

The whole crowd cheered when Lena crossed the finish line first, but she was not looking at the clock or her medal. Her eyes searched the stands until they landed on an empty seat in the front row, and her smile faded just a little.

What can you infer from Lena's reaction at the finish line?
A) She is unhappy that she won the race
B) She wished someone important to her had come to watch
C) She does not like crowds
D) She forgot she was racing
items.answer: B) She wished someone important to her had come to watch

steps: Lena wins but ignores the clock and medal.
She searches for someone and her smile fades at an "empty seat."
That suggests she wished a certain person had come, choice B.
solution.answer: B) She wished someone important to her had come to watch

items.prompt:
Read the fable.

A dog carrying a bone saw his own reflection in a pond and thought it was another dog with a bigger bone. He barked to grab it and dropped his own bone into the water, losing everything.

What is the theme of this fable?
A) Dogs like bones
B) Being greedy for more can cost you what you already have
C) Ponds are dangerous
D) Barking is loud
items.answer: B) Being greedy for more can cost you what you already have

steps: The dog wants the bigger bone in the reflection.
By grabbing for it, he drops his real bone.
The lesson is that greed can cost you what you have, choice B.
solution.answer: B) Being greedy for more can cost you what you already have

items.prompt:
Read the story.

Everyone told Amina she was too young to start a recycling club. She started it anyway, with just two members. She kept showing up, week after week, and by the end of the year the whole school was recycling and her club had fifty kids.

Which sentence best states the theme?
A) Recycling is good for the earth
B) A determined person can make a big difference, no matter their age
C) Clubs need fifty members
D) Young people cannot lead
items.answer: B) A determined person can make a big difference, no matter their age

steps: Amina is told she is too young but starts the club anyway.
Her persistence grows it to fifty members.
The theme is that determination makes a difference regardless of age, choice B.
solution.answer: B) A determined person can make a big difference, no matter their age

items.prompt:
Read the story.

Rafael spent weeks building a birdhouse for the contest. His younger brother wanted to help but kept getting in the way. Instead of shooing him off, Rafael handed him the sandpaper and taught him to smooth the edges. Their birdhouse did not win, but the brothers hung it in the yard and watched a family of wrens move in.

Which sentence best summarizes the story?
A) Rafael wins the birdhouse contest by himself
B) Rafael includes his little brother in building a birdhouse that later becomes a home for wrens
C) Rafael refuses to let his brother help and builds alone
D) The birdhouse falls apart in the yard
items.answer: B) Rafael includes his little brother in building a birdhouse that later becomes a home for wrens

steps: A summary states the main events truthfully.
Rafael lets his brother help, they do not win, but wrens move into the birdhouse.
Choice B matches; the others change the facts.
solution.answer: B) Rafael includes his little brother in building a birdhouse that later becomes a home for wrens

items.prompt:
Read the story.

The merchant offered the traveler a room made of gold or a plain room with a window facing the sea. The traveler chose the plain room. Each morning he woke to the sound of waves and the rising sun, while the merchant, surrounded by gold, complained he could never sleep for worrying someone would steal it.

Which theme is best supported by the story?
A) Gold rooms are uncomfortable
B) Simple things can bring more peace than riches
C) Travelers should sleep near the sea
D) Merchants are dishonest
items.answer: B) Simple things can bring more peace than riches

steps: The traveler picks the plain room and enjoys the sea and sunrise.
The rich merchant cannot sleep for worrying about his gold.
The theme is that simple things bring more peace than riches, choice B.
solution.answer: B) Simple things can bring more peace than riches

items.prompt:
Read the story.

When the class pet gerbil escaped, everyone panicked and chased it, but Nina crouched quietly, held out a sunflower seed, and waited. The gerbil crept right into her open hand.

Which word best describes Nina?
A) Loud
B) Patient
C) Careless
D) Angry

steps: While others chase and panic, Nina stays still and waits.
She holds out a seed and lets the gerbil come.
That shows she is patient, choice B.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

The abandoned amusement park was silent now. Rust crept up the once-bright carousel, weeds curled around the ticket booth, and a torn flag flapped over the empty roller coaster. Somewhere, a loose chain clinked in the wind.

Which phrase best describes the mood the setting creates?
A) Cheerful and exciting
B) Lonely and eerie
C) Warm and cozy
D) Busy and crowded

steps: The park is silent, rusted, and overgrown with weeds.
A torn flag and a clinking chain add to the emptiness.
These details create a lonely, eerie mood, choice B.

items.prompt:
Read the story.

At the start of the year, Theo never spoke in class and hid behind his hair when called on. But he joined the drama club, practiced his lines every night, and by the spring play he stood center stage and delivered his part in a clear, strong voice.

How does Theo change over the course of the story?
A) He becomes shyer than before
B) He grows from shy and quiet to confident
C) He quits the drama club
D) He stays exactly the same
items.answer: B) He grows from shy and quiet to confident

steps: At the start Theo never speaks and hides behind his hair.
He practices and by spring speaks in a "clear, strong voice" on stage.
So he changes from shy to confident, choice B.
solution.answer: B) He grows from shy and quiet to confident

items.prompt:
Read the story.

Mr. Halloran was known as the grumpiest neighbor on the block, forever grumbling about noise and shooing kids off his lawn. But when the youngest child on the street lost her kitten, it was Mr. Halloran who searched the alleys past midnight, knocked on every door, and finally returned the kitten wrapped in his own scarf. "Do not tell anyone," he grumbled, but he was smiling.

What does the story reveal about Mr. Halloran's true character?
A) He is exactly as grumpy and unkind as he seems
B) Beneath his grumpy manner, he is caring and kind
C) He dislikes all animals
D) He never helps anyone
items.answer: B) Beneath his grumpy manner, he is caring and kind

steps: Mr. Halloran seems grumpy, grumbling and shooing kids away.
But he searches past midnight and returns the kitten in his own scarf.
This reveals he is kind beneath his grumpy manner, choice B.
solution.answer: B) Beneath his grumpy manner, he is caring and kind
